neutrality_rule: Candidate records are exploratory predictions. No score, pass count, ordering, or signature distance is a ranking.

candidates.title: Predictive-Quotient Bisimulation

candidates.title: Full C-Package Staged Handoff

candidates.title: Causal-Overlap Process Continuation
candidates.one_sentence: Structural continuation is an uninterrupted causally coupled process whose operational responsibility moves across distinct supports, not a matched endpoint reconstructed after the process stops.
candidates.common_type: A changing-support process history H over a joint time/order base with source and target support projections.
candidates.bridge_signature: O = (H, supp(t), coupling(t), responsibility(t)) with nonzero causal/process overlap and target takeover.
candidates.bridge_data: stage histories; causal dependencies; support shares; responsibility map; handoff completion and withdrawal events
candidates.admissibility: No stage gap in the selected process; overlap carries the named process invariant; source/target labels do not define continuity.
candidates.exact_invariants: selected process organization and causal update relation through every overlap stage
candidates.allowed_variation: component identity, support allocation, representation, and local timing within the process connection
candidates.approximate_version: A process-simulation tube with lower bounds on coupling/organizational continuity and explicit gap tolerance only if separately defined.
candidates.route_policy: Replacement order can matter; process continuity is route-specific unless all critical pairs commute on the selected organization.
candidates.loop_test: Compare two replacement schedules and their intermediate causal organizations, not only final states.
candidates.composition_rule: Concatenate overlap histories only when the terminal mixed process of one leg is the initial process of the next.
candidates.copy_rule: A detached copy is a new target process; if a continuous process genuinely forks, the lineage relation branches from the fork.
candidates.fission_rule: Branch-valued only for a causally continuous fork, not for independent reconstruction from a record.
candidates.fusion_rule: Requires an actual coupled process merger; endpoint state fusion alone is insufficient.
candidates.deletion_rule: Deleting the source after a detached copy does not retroactively create process continuity.
candidates.empty_condition: No target process lies on an uninterrupted admissible moving-support history.
candidates.target_scope: A target-native ongoing process; the full C-package is an optional stronger audit.
candidates.source_status: Finite process stipulated for exploration, not an actual conscious source.
candidates.target_status: Target must continue the selected process and later operate without source/bridge support.
candidates.support_stages: The process may straddle X_S and X_T during overlap; final responsibility lies on X_T.
candidates.clocks: A shared partial order across coupled events is required; identical rates are not.
candidates.hiddenness: Operational causal organization may be privileged and is not inferred from public smoothness.
candidates.action_credit: Only preserved if causal provenance flows through the overlap; copied credit labels do not suffice.
candidates.temporal_closure: Uninterrupted event order is central; dormant gaps are excluded in the strict version.
candidates.recombination: Fork and merge points are explicit process events, with no automatic global glue.
candidates.viability: The strict handoff additionally requires target operation after source withdrawal, but process lineage and autonomy stay separate lanes.
candidates.removal: Withdraw all source-side process contributions and the migration controller after the takeover boundary.
candidates.autonomy_horizon: At least one full endogenous maintenance/update cycle, extended to an invariant region when available.
candidates.recognition: Finite toys expose causal graphs and support allocation; empirical use would require interventionally identified causal organization.
candidates.false_surfaces: Smooth replay, detached exact copy, externally scheduled target, or overlap that transmits only a public shadow.
candidates.new_terms: moving-support process history; responsibility-transfer map; continuous-fork lineage; process takeover gate

candidates.negative_control: S02 destructive scan with no live overlap.

candidates.deletion_rule: Deletion removes active branches but does not rewrite the prior category or select one successor.
candidates.empty_condition: No admissible target object/morphism receives the source history under F.
candidates.target_scope: A globally coherent event/history package; full C-package and autonomy are separate.
candidates.source_status: Finite event category stipulated or mined from a toy.
candidates.target_status: Target event/history category must be target-native after any bridge withdrawal for an A claim.
candidates.support_stages: Events name their supporting carrier tokens; mixed-support events are explicit objects, not implicit identities.
candidates.clocks: Partial order and route composition are preserved; rate equality is unnecessary.
candidates.hiddenness: Recombination and loop probes may be unavailable at public interfaces.
candidates.action_credit: Can be included as event labels but is not automatic.
candidates.temporal_closure: Represented through event order and composition; full target temporal minting remains a separate audit.
candidates.removal: Remove bridge event generator and source-supported morphisms; test whether the target category/dynamics persists.
candidates.autonomy_horizon: Not built into the exact functor; a separate finite horizon or invariant region is required.
candidates.recognition: Requires intermediate route records and joint recombination probes, not endpoint-only tests.
candidates.false_surfaces: Branchwise agreement with wrong joins, locally admissible edges without global event, and endpoint-restoring holonomy.
candidates.new_terms: heterogeneous continuation functor; recombination-preserving lineage; route-loop action; defect-enriched branch functor
candidates.theorem_shapes: Functorial branch/fusion classification; flatness/confluence criterion; local-global event obstruction; recombination separation theorem.
candidates.no_go_shapes: Endpoint and branchwise summaries cannot determine recombination/holonomy; local edges do not force a global event.
candidates.toys: small event categories with fork/join; same endpoints with different loop actions; local edge triangle with failed cocycle; branch marginal counterfeit.
candidates.positive_control: S09 fission with explicit shared-prefix branches and S18 flat round trip.
candidates.negative_control: S31 event package assembled from locally admissible edges but no global object.
candidates.adversarial: S24 many-to-many reconfiguration stresses relation composition and global glue.
candidates.falsifier: F preserves listed local maps but fails composition/recombination on a generated diagram, or a purported flatness basis misses a route loop.
candidates.minimal_model: A finite fork–join category with two route loops, one marked recombination map, and a target category with a controlled mismatch.
candidates.implementation_dependencies: finite categories/graphs, relation composition, critical-pair and loop enumeration
candidates.kill_criteria: Category presentation encodes desired ancestry labels; no finite generator basis captures relevant routes; functoriality is too weak to discriminate copies.
candidates.nonclaims: No full package or autonomy by default; no personal identity; no consciousness; no empirical route access.
candidates.ontological_boundary: Relation-valued structural ancestry remains below personal identity even if A1/A2-P are accepted.

candidates.title: Reflexive Temporal–Credit Ledger Bridge
candidates.one_sentence: Continuation preserves a source-specific reflexive self-coordinate, package-minted temporal order, and action-credit ledger through a typed clock/provenance bridge, allowing branches but rejecting externally scripted replicas.
candidates.common_type: A history/ledger comparison object with clock connection and provenance morphisms.
candidates.bridge_data: self-coordinate histories; event order; local clocks; action-credit records; minting authorities; branch prefixes
candidates.admissibility: Clock and ledger mappings are nonretroactive, symmetry-respecting, and distinguish copied labels from endogenous updates.
candidates.exact_invariants: self-update relation, temporal order up to admitted reparameterization, credit provenance, and shared-prefix branch history
candidates.allowed_variation: clock rate, implementation, representation, and post-branch new credit events
candidates.approximate_version: Vector defect for phase/order, self-update, credit provenance, and ledger reconciliation, with hard nonretroactivity gates.
candidates.route_policy: Order strongly matters; route independence is not expected when replacement order changes credit or phase history.
candidates.loop_test: Round-trip the ledger and compare phase, minted order, self-coordinate, and credit ancestry.
candidates.composition_rule: Compose only when clock maps are monotone and ledger authorities/provenance align; retain branch prefixes.
candidates.copy_rule: Copies share a prefix and become distinct ledger branches; no branch is uniquely selected by later deletion.
candidates.fission_rule: Branch-valued with a common prefix and branch-local subsequent credit.
candidates.fusion_rule: Fusion is underdetermined or blocked unless conflicting self/credit histories admit an explicit reconciliation law.
candidates.deletion_rule: Deletion removes a branch but cannot alter prior shared-prefix classification.
candidates.empty_condition: No target history carries an admissible self/clock/credit continuation from the source prefix.
candidates.target_scope: A historical self/temporal/credit core, not the entire C-package.
candidates.source_status: Finite ledger history stipulated; no metaphysical self is assumed.
candidates.target_status: Target must generate new order, self-updates, and credit under target authority after withdrawal.
candidates.support_stages: Ledger records may be mirrored during overlap; minting authority and active update support are named at each stage.
candidates.clocks: Monotone reparameterization is allowed; external phase service is not target-native closure.
candidates.hiddenness: Ledger and self-update structure may be privileged and can differ behind identical reports.
candidates.recombination: Shared-prefix branches and any fusion reconciliation are explicit.
candidates.viability: Not core, but withdrawal may expose inability to mint/update the ledger.
candidates.removal: Remove source clock, scheduler, ledger service, bridge synchronizer, and source minting authority.
candidates.autonomy_horizon: Long enough for at least one target-native self-update, temporal cycle, and credited action.
candidates.recognition: Privileged ledger/clock audits in toys; empirical recognition would require provenance-secure instruments.
candidates.false_surfaces: Copied autobiographical text, externally scheduled timing, replayed actions, and stale backups.
candidates.new_terms: self-coordinate bridge; clock connection; credit-provenance morphism; shared-prefix ledger lineage
candidates.theorem_shapes: Ledger-preservation theorem; clock-reparameterization invariance; nonretroactivity under deletion; fusion-reconciliation classification.
candidates.no_go_shapes: Endpoint copies and external schedulers cannot establish target-native temporal/credit continuation.
candidates.toys: finite ledgers with branch prefixes; radical clock rescaling; external scheduler counterfeit; stale backup; conflicting fusion records.
candidates.positive_control: S19 with a lawful monotone clock translation and target-native ledger updates.
candidates.negative_control: S29 external scheduler masquerading as temporal closure.
candidates.adversarial: S10/S23 fusion of conflicting credit histories.
candidates.falsifier: The bridge accepts a target whose credit is minted by the source/scheduler or violates monotone/nonretroactive ledger constraints.
candidates.minimal_model: Two finite event/ledger systems with a clock rescaling, one branching prefix, one external scheduler, and one stale checkpoint.
candidates.implementation_dependencies: finite partial orders, ledger provenance, monotone maps, branch/fusion checks
candidates.kill_criteria: Ledger variables are only copied labels; provenance cannot be defined noncircularly; clock translation is arbitrary enough to trivialize tests.
candidates.nonclaims: No full package; no unique continuer; no claim that memory text equals self; no consciousness; no personal identity.
candidates.ontological_boundary: The structural self/ledger relation requires H-IDENTITY-O for any personal survival reading.

candidates.title: Residual-Bounded Predictive Simulation Bundle
candidates.one_sentence: A target carries a deliberately minimal predictive–historical–viability bundle when an explicit vector residual remains below justified margins under composition and withdrawal.
candidates.common_type: A probe-indexed bundle specification with vector metric and hard gates.
candidates.bridge_kind: residual-bounded forward simulation with hard-gate vector
candidates.bridge_data: probe family; predictive transitions; selected historical/gluing tests; viability margins; defect composition law
candidates.admissibility: Features and thresholds are fixed from counterexamples or stability margins, not desired scenario labels; omitted dimensions are explicit.
candidates.exact_invariants: The zero-residual finite core and every declared hard gate
candidates.allowed_variation: bounded deviations in soft coordinates within a stated horizon and perturbation family
candidates.approximate_version: Defining form: Delta<=epsilon componentwise, epsilon below named stability/viability margins.
candidates.route_policy: Route defects accumulate by a declared nonlinear law; route-independent labels require all relevant loop defects below margin.
candidates.loop_test: Measure vector residual after closed routes and compare each hard-gate coordinate rather than one average fidelity.
candidates.composition_rule: Compose simulations with an explicit bound F(Delta_1,Delta_2); reject if any hard gate or margin is crossed.
candidates.copy_rule: Every qualifying source-derived copy can be a branch; small defect never selects a unique person.
candidates.fission_rule: Branch-valued while every branch remains inside the declared bundle margins.
candidates.fusion_rule: Fusion-valued or underdetermined depending on whether histories/gates admit one bounded merged bundle.
candidates.deletion_rule: Deletion does not lower residual or create lineage.
candidates.empty_condition: No target state/history satisfies all hard gates and componentwise margins.
candidates.target_scope: A minimal bundle selected to preserve corpus discriminators, explicitly not assumed equivalent to C1–C8.
candidates.source_status: Finite bundle stipulated and fully observable in toy models.
candidates.target_status: Target must satisfy the residual and hard-gate contract; autonomy is separately tested.
candidates.support_stages: Bundle components name their support and may migrate at different stages; a global compatibility gate is retained.
candidates.clocks: Time reparameterization contributes a temporal residual rather than being silently ignored.
candidates.hiddenness: Probe completeness is a declared limitation; public-only probes cannot close the hidden residual.
candidates.action_credit: Included as a selected hard or soft coordinate when the candidate uses it; omission is visible.
candidates.temporal_closure: Represented by selected history/clock tests and a hard external-scheduler control.
candidates.recombination: Included through a gluing/recombination residual when branch scenarios are in scope.
candidates.viability: Margin to viability boundary is explicit and controls approximation.
candidates.removal: Remove source, bridge, decoder, external scheduler, and repair service; recompute residual under target dynamics.
candidates.autonomy_horizon: Declared finite horizon plus margin; an invariant-region version is a stronger theorem target.
candidates.recognition: Finite probe battery with complete toy-state access and declared false-positive/negative surface.
candidates.false_surfaces: High average fidelity hiding a hard-gate failure; thresholds tuned post hoc; residual small only while source remains connected.
candidates.new_terms: continuation-bundle residual; hard-gate vector; margin-indexed lineage relation; residual composition law
candidates.theorem_shapes: Finite exact core; perturbation/stability theorem away from boundaries; defect-composition theorem; counterexample-driven minimality theorem.
candidates.no_go_shapes: Scalar fidelity cannot guarantee every critical gate; no uniform approximation theorem holds at zero viability/branch margin.
candidates.toys: finite bundle with predictive, ledger, glue, and viability bits; noisy bridge; high-average hard-gate counterfeit; two-stage residual accumulation.
candidates.positive_control: S17 or S25 inside a proved error/viability margin.
candidates.negative_control: S16 at a threshold crossing and S30 certificate-only mismatch.
candidates.adversarial: S32 approximately reversible round trip with accumulated residual.
candidates.falsifier: A below-threshold bridge crosses a declared hard gate or a purported composition bound is violated by a finite counterexample.
candidates.minimal_model: A pair of 4–8 state systems with four defect coordinates, one hard gate, one viability margin, and two composable bridges.
candidates.implementation_dependencies: finite transition systems, vector metrics, exhaustive counterexample search, simple optimization
candidates.kill_criteria: Bundle selection is ad hoc; no stable margins exist; defect law grows too fast for any nontrivial multi-stage bridge.
candidates.nonclaims: No claim the bundle is sufficient for consciousness or personal identity; no scalar sameness score; no general continuum theorem.
candidates.ontological_boundary: A1/A2-P and H-IDENTITY-O are not part of the residual theorem and cannot be encoded by a small epsilon.

candidates.title: Heterogeneous Predictive-Ancestry Relation
candidates.one_sentence: The primary cross-carrier object is a route-scoped relation among predictive histories, generalized to distinct carrier types and allowed to return one successor, many branches, fusion predecessors, no target, or underdetermination.
candidates.common_type: A typed route record and a relation L_ST subset PredHist(X_S) x PredHist(X_T).
candidates.bridge_signature: L_B(h_S,h_T) iff an admissible cross-carrier route carries the declared predictive ancestry witness from h_S to h_T.
candidates.bridge_kind: branch-valued history relation, retyping predictive ancestry rather than transporting a state token
candidates.bridge_data: source/target predictive histories; route; ancestry witness; branch/fusion graph; empty-target condition
candidates.admissibility: Witness uses predictive/route facts rather than target names or desired identity labels; symmetry is preserved.
candidates.exact_invariants: the declared predictive ancestry relation and its branch/fusion structure
candidates.allowed_variation: target implementation, nonlineage package features, and post-branch divergence
candidates.approximate_version: Open: either a graded ancestry witness or a robust classification away from relation bifurcations; not assumed.
candidates.route_policy: Lineage is route-scoped; route-independent ancestry is a stronger flatness theorem.
candidates.loop_test: Compare ancestry relations generated by alternative routes and record nontrivial loop action.
candidates.composition_rule: Relational composition with retained intermediate route witnesses; special rules are required for fission followed by fusion.
candidates.copy_rule: Nondestructive qualifying copies are branches; source persistence is compatible with plural succession.
candidates.fusion_rule: Fusion-valued with multiple predecessors when one target predictive history lawfully receives them.
candidates.deletion_rule: Deletion never selects one branch and does not retroactively alter ancestry.
candidates.empty_condition: The predictive target set on the declared route is empty or every candidate target fails the ancestry witness.
candidates.target_scope: Target package realization is deliberately bracketed and reported as a separate lane, often not applicable to this schema.
candidates.source_status: A finite source predictive history is stipulated; no consciousness claim.
candidates.target_status: Only the target history needed for ancestry is required; full package/autonomy are separate.
candidates.support_stages: Route records name source, bridge, and target history types at each stage.
candidates.clocks: Partial orders and dormant records are explicit route data; a gap is not automatically fatal or preserving.
candidates.hiddenness: Predictive ancestry may require privileged history access; public reports are insufficient.
candidates.action_credit: Not part of the base relation and therefore a known incompleteness exposed by TS-08/TS-02.
candidates.temporal_closure: Route order is represented, but full target temporal closure is not claimed.
candidates.recombination: Fission/fusion relations are explicit; richer recombination structure is deferred to TS-07.
candidates.viability: Can produce an empty target if a route-specific target predicate fails, but target autonomy is not built in.
candidates.removal: Autonomy is tested independently; lineage relation can hold even when a target later fails maintenance.
candidates.autonomy_horizon: Not defined by the ancestry criterion; scenario-specific A labels remain separate.
candidates.recognition: Finite toys expose routes and predictive histories; empirical use needs a history-sensitive recognition bridge.
candidates.false_surfaces: Independent structural twins, public-perfect predictive counterfeits, and symmetry-breaking by labels or later deletion.
candidates.new_terms: heterogeneous predictive ancestry; route witness; branch-valued target set; cross-carrier empty-target relation
candidates.theorem_shapes: Retyped ancestry classification; relational composition; symmetry/nonunique-continuation theorem; fission/fusion laws.
candidates.no_go_shapes: No symmetry-respecting structural rule can select exactly one of two identical equally related targets; target equivalence without route gives no ancestry.
candidates.toys: finite predictive histories with destructive reconstruction, symmetric duplication, fission/fusion, independent twin, and stale backup.
candidates.positive_control: S09 fission with common predictive ancestry and divergent futures.
candidates.adversarial: S10 fission then fusion stresses composition and predecessor conflict.
candidates.falsifier: The relation chooses one target in a symmetry-preserving duplicate or composes through a route whose intermediate witness is absent.
candidates.minimal_model: A finite route graph with two carrier-typed predictive state spaces, a split, a merge, an empty target, and an independent twin.
candidates.implementation_dependencies: finite relations, predictive quotients, route graphs, relational composition
candidates.kill_criteria: Ancestry witness is circular; relation becomes universal; composition cannot distinguish independent twins or stale epochs.
candidates.nonclaims: No target C-package, autonomy, consciousness, unique personal identity, or approximate identity claim.
candidates.ontological_boundary: H-IDENTITY-O is explicitly required for any personal-identity reading; A1/A2-P do not select branches.
